question_or_symptom: A doorbell request can be sent successfully while its ACK is lost, delayed behind a completion, or replaced by a timeout or cancellation outcome.
observation: The server may already have admitted the command when the client cannot validate its ACK. Treating that state as an ordinary retry can duplicate mutation, while consuming a completion before its ACK destroys the protocol commit order.
conclusion: Queue admission ACK and asynchronous completion are separate commit boundaries, and ambiguity before a canonical ACK is not recoverable within the same session.
decision: Require ACK before completion. Poison and close the runtime instance after any post-send timeout, cancellation, EOF, malformed response, identity mismatch, or early completion before a canonical ACK. Keep an already acknowledged pending command intact when completion wait alone times out or is cancelled so the caller can retry the wait without replaying the doorbell.
invalidated_assumptions: A timed-out queue request can always be retried safely on the same connection.
Receiving the completion proves that an omitted or malformed ACK can be ignored.
